english: Let $H$ be the hyperbola with centre at the origin and transverse axis along the $x$-axis whose eccentricity is $2$ and whose two directrices are at a distance $2$ from each other. Let $S$ be the focus of $H$ lying on the negative $x$-axis, and let $C$ be the parabola whose focus is $S$ and whose directrix is the directrix of $H$ lying in the half-plane $x>0$. Then the sum of the abscissae of all the points common to $H$ and $C$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $H$ वह अतिपरवलय है जिसका केन्द्र मूलबिन्दु पर है, अनुप्रस्थ अक्ष $x$-अक्ष के अनुदिश है, उत्केन्द्रता $2$ है तथा जिसकी दोनों नियता रेखाओं के बीच की दूरी $2$ है। माना कि $S$, $H$ की वह नाभि है जो ऋणात्मक $x$-अक्ष पर स्थित है, तथा $C$ वह परवलय है जिसकी नाभि $S$ है और जिसकी नियता रेखा $H$ की वह नियता रेखा है जो अर्धतल $x>0$ में स्थित है। तब $H$ तथा $C$ के सभी उभयनिष्ठ बिन्दुओं के भुजों का योग ______ है।
solution_full: Let $H:\ \dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$. Its directrices are $x=\pm\dfrac{a}{e}$, so the distance between them is $\dfrac{2a}{e}=a=2$ (as $e=2$).
Then $c=ae=4$ and $b^{2}=a^{2}(e^{2}-1)=4\cdot3=12$. So $H:\ \dfrac{x^{2}}{4}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{12}=1$, the foci are $(\pm4,0)$, and the directrices are $x=\pm1$.

$S=(-4,0)$ and the directrix of $C$ is $x=1$. A point $(x,y)$ lies on $C$ when its distance from $S$ equals its distance from $x=1$: $(x+4)^{2}+y^{2}=(x-1)^{2}$, i.e. $y^{2}=-10x-15=-10\left(x+\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$. (Vertex $\left(-\dfrac{3}{2},0\right)$, opening to the left; on $C$, $x\leq-\dfrac{3}{2}$.)
$x=-\dfrac{1}{3}$ gives $y^{2}=\dfrac{10}{3}-15<0$: no real point (indeed $-\dfrac{1}{3}>-\dfrac{3}{2}$ is outside $C$).
$x=-3$ gives $y^{2}=15$: the two points $(-3,\sqrt{15})$ and $(-3,-\sqrt{15})$. Check on $H$: $\dfrac{9}{4}-\dfrac{15}{12}=1$.
Sum of the abscissae of all common points $=(-3)+(-3)=-6$.
originality_note: New: a parabola built from one focus of a hyperbola and the directrix belonging to the other focus, so that the hyperbola must first be fixed from e and the directrix distance, and the meeting points come with a spurious root and a double count (way 5). Closest known: textbook exercises on foci and directrices of x^2/a^2 - y^2/b^2 = 1, and 2026-P2-Q13 (hyperbola sharing foci with an ellipse, meeting a parabola). Different because: the parabola is defined by mixed elements of the hyperbola, and the answer depends on rejecting x = -1/3 and counting both symmetric points.

concept_use.Basic elements of the standard parabola:: The parabola is written from its focus S(-4, 0) and directrix x = 1 by the focus-directrix definition (vertex (-3/2, 0), 4a = 10).
concept_use.Basic elements of the standard hyperbola: The hyperbola is fixed from e = 2 and the distance 2a/e = 2 between its directrices: a = 2, b^2 = 12, foci (±4, 0), directrices x = ±1.

stem_review: Read as a student: every curve and point is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and checked by an independent numerical route, is unique and matches the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked that 'distance between directrices' and 'directrix in x > 0' identify the lines uniquely, that x = -1/3 gives no real point, and that both points with x = -3 are counted; -6 is a negative integer as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: Fixing H from e and the directrix distance, building C from mixed focus/directrix, and rejecting the spurious root while counting both symmetric points.
justification: Several standard stages chained (hyperbola from e and directrices, parabola from focus-directrix, intersection) with a trap at the end, in numerical format with no options. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q13 (L3), a numerical question combining hyperbola elements with a parabola.
